claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by understanding your situation. To determine your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to know about the child or children you're claiming for.

**First question: How old is the child (or what are the ages of the children) you're claiming for?**

Please tell me:
- The child's name and age, or
- If you have multiple children, their names and ages

This will help me understand which eligibility rules apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex - he's 13 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for that information! So we're assessing Child Benefit eligibility for **Alex, who is 13 years old**.

Since Alex is under 16, he automatically qualifies as a "qualifying child" for Child Benefit purposes. Now I need to check a few more things to confirm your overall eligibility.

Let me move forward with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex working, and if so, is he working less than 24 hours per week?**

(Note: This check is primarily for children aged 16 and over, but let me confirm for completeness - is Alex in any paid work at all, or is he not working?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's still in school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! So Alex is not working and is still in school. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving any of these benefits in his own right?**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

(In other words, is he not claiming any of these benefits for himself?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't get any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex doesn't receive those benefits in his own name. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex in an apprenticeship?**

Since he's still in school at age 13, I suspect the answer is no - but let me confirm to be thorough.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship - he's just doing regular school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in regular school, not an apprenticeship. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Now I need to check your residency status.** This is about where *you* (the claimant/parent) normally live, not Alex.

Could you tell me:
- **Do you normally live in the UK?**

If yes, that's all I need to know and we can proceed. If no, please let me know your situation so I can check if any special circumstances apply (such as EU Settlement Scheme status, or working abroad as a Crown servant, etc.).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK - I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, I need to check if any special circumstances apply that would still make you eligible. Let me ask you some clarifying questions:

**Could you tell me:**

1. **Which country are you living in?**

2. **Do you have any of the following statuses?**
   - Settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
   - Pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
   - Are you a Crown servant (working for the UK government) living abroad?

3. **If you have pre-settled status, are you:**
   - Working and earning above the National Insurance threshold?
   - Actively seeking work?
   - Studying with sufficient financial resources?
   - A family member of an EEA or Swiss national with a right to reside?
   - Supporting yourself and your family with sufficient resources (and NOT claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit)?

This information will help me determine if you meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm living in France at the moment. I don't have any of those statuses - no settled or pre-settled status, and I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I'm just living abroad.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Thank you for clarifying that. Based on what you've told me, you don't normally live in the UK and you don't fall into any of the special circumstances that would allow eligibility for Child Benefit while living abroad (such as EU Settlement Scheme status, Crown servant status, etc.).

Unfortunately, this means you would not meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit.

Let me confirm this is the correct outcome by navigating through the system:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me provide you with the formal eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## **Your Child Benefit Eligibility Result: INELIGIBLE**

### Summary:
Unfortunately, you are **not eligible for Child Benefit** for Alex because you don't meet the UK residency requirements.

### Reason:
- **Alex's situation:** Alex is 13 years old and meets all the individual requirements for Child Benefit - he's under 16, not working full-time, not receiving disqualifying benefits, and not in a disqualifying apprenticeship. ✓
  
- **Your situation:** However, you do not normally live in the UK. Additionally, you don't have any of the special qualifying statuses that would allow you to claim Child Benefit while living abroad (such as EU Settlement Scheme settled/pre-settled status, or Crown servant status).

### What this means:
The residency requirement is a fundamental eligibility criterion for Child Benefit. To be eligible, you must either:
- Normally live in the UK, OR
- Have one of the qualifying statuses that permits claiming from abroad

### Next Steps:
If your circumstances change (for example, if you return to the UK or acquire settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme), you may become eligible at that time. You can always reapply if your situation changes.

For more information, you can visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

Is there anything else I can help you with regarding this assessment?

reasonings: Alex is 13 years old and meets all the child-specific requirements for Child Benefit: he is under 16, not working full-time, not receiving disqualifying benefits in his own right, and not in a disqualifying apprenticeship. The claimant is living in France without any of the qualifying statuses (such as settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme or Crown servant status) that would permit them to claim Child Benefit from abroad. Without meeting the residency requirement, the claim cannot proceed regardless of the child's eligibility.

The residency requirement is a fundamental eligibility criterion that must be met."
